::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 7th [1899]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels/85
:::

My dear [C C](people/person_329.qmd)
It is a cruel stroke to lose Lanty at the same time as [M P](organizations/other_52.qmd) You must feel desolate like Othello.  [Aimée Leroy](people/person_869.qmd) has an idea, and may write to you about it, anent M P  She says she has seen [A D I](people/person_744.qmd)’s business advertised to be sold.[^1]  I have not, but I think my notice was sent in time.  He has taken no notice, I suppose he washes his hands of all of us.

I shall be quite open to you and glad any day before the 16th when [Helen](people/person_1613.qmd) comes to me – I believe-  [Annie Moberly](people/person_1024.qmd) comes on the 12th, for about a week.  It would be good to talk over Arthurine with her.[^2]  Helen may come a day or two later /than 16\\, but I will find out and how about space will then appear  I do want a talk but you had better see Aimée first.  I though [Mary Bramston](people/person_198.qmd) was from home, but no doubt it is only for a day or two.  I should be very glad of a talk.  So much coming at once on you.

[Henry Bowles](people/person_184.qmd) was surprised by the gift of a cruet (ecclesiastical) from his choir the other day

your affte
C M Yonge

What becomes of stock of [Constant Prince](other_books/otherbook_741.qmd)

---

[^1]: The question was whether it would be possible to revive the *Monthly Packet*, which had disappeared with the collapse of Innes's business.
[^2]: Arthurine was a character in 'Come to her Kingdom' (collected in *More Bywords*), who was to reappear in the character of a moderate feminist in CMY's next novel *Modern Broods*.
